subject: Run-of-show + environment notes for Elaine Chen — ML coding screen
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Scheduling: Elaine Chen — ML coding (live)

Hi team,

Elaine is confirmed for a 60-minute ML coding screen on Thu 17 Sep at 10:30am PT. Panel: Karthik (modeling), Marcus (systems/infra), Kimberly (debrief). Chloe — can you own the run-of-show and the ephemeral environment links?

Candidate details: Elaine Chen, ex-ML infra at ExaCorp, prefers 11am PT but able to move to 10:30 if needed. She asked about timeboxed feedback and whether we can provide a small README for the sandbox.

Quick asks:
- Chloe: link to session and ephemeral VM + any special instructions for KV cache / LRU test case (Marcus is using a micro-benchmark).
- Karthik: two prompt-based tasks (one model correctness, one performance edge case).
- Marcus: confirm access to internal codestash and that session has network egress blocked.

Attachments: candidate-consent.txt (signed)

Thanks,
Kimberly
Recruiting Operations
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: candidate-consent.txt (text) ---

From: chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduling: Elaine Chen — ML coding (live)

Thanks Kim — taking ownership.

Run-of-show (high level):
- 10:20am PT: interviewer join + tech check (audio, shared pad)
- 10:30am PT: intro (5m) / expectations / consent note
- 10:35am PT: coding task 1 (30m) — live on ephemeral notebook; candidate gets 25m + 5m follow-up Q
- 11:05am PT: short systems micro-benchmark (10m) run by Marcus
- 11:15am PT: debrief 15m (internal) — candidate off call

Environment notes:
- Using ephemeral sandbox (ENV-712) with preloaded dataset and a lightly instrumented KV cache. No outbound network; we provide a token-limited S3 stub for loading test assets.
- Candidate will be given a temporary CoderPad session: https://coderpad.io/session/RED-9834
- Quick-read: coding-env-readme.pdf attached — includes how to run the micro-benchmark and where logs are written (/tmp/infra-check.log).

Marcus — I toggled the LRU cache to smaller capacity for the benchmark case (to exercise cache eviction). If you want other knobs (quantize path, kernel selection), call them out and I’ll add to README.

Elaine — if you have any special editor preferences (vim/emacs/VSCode), tell me and we’ll configure the ephemeral env. Also let me know if 10:30am is still OK or if you prefer 11am.

Attachments: run_of_show.md, coding-env-readme.pdf

See you all on the bridge — Chloe
Staff Recruiting Coordinator, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: run_of_show.md (text) ---
--- Attachment: coding-env-readme.pdf (pdf) ---

From: Elaine Chen <elaine.chen@gmail.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scheduling: Elaine Chen — ML coding (live)

Thanks — 10:30am PT works for me if you need the earlier slot. A couple of quick notes: I use VSCode (remote) but I can adapt to whatever the sandbox exposes. Two small asks:

1) Will the ephemeral env allow short-lived internet access to pip-install trivial libs (requests/numpy)? If not, I can vendor the few files.
2) I have an accommodation request: prefer a 5-minute break in the middle (after the first 20–25 minutes) to stretch and reopen the session.

Appreciate the transparency on the KV cache — sounds good.

Best,
Elaine
elaine.chen@gmail.com

Perfect — I’ll run the micro-benchmark and watch KV eviction behaviors. Notes for the panel:
- I will use the infra probe that writes /tmp/infra-check.log and then snapshot the environment; please do not purge logs until 1pm PT.
- Chloe: please ensure the CoderPad session has write access to /tmp and that logs are persisted to the sandbox share (we'll pull after debrief).
- Karthik: I flagged two edge cases in the run_of_show.md under "Benchmark knobs" — one exercises a long sequence (attention blowup), the other a small-batch throughput path.

Elaine — noted on the 5-minute break. We'll add a 3–5 minute midpoint pause immediately after the first coding block. Regarding pip installs: we allow wheel installs from the internal mirror only for a small whitelist. If you need numpy/requests we can pre-stage them; please tell us now and we’ll add to the sandbox image.

See you in a bit.
Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
